requirements.title: C_F_PROCPOINTER argument restrictions
requirements.definition: CPTR is a scalar C_FUNPTR INTENT(IN) value denoting an interoperable C procedure address or a C_FUNLOC result; FPTR is an INTENT(OUT) procedure pointer that is not a component of a coindexed object and whose interface is interoperable with, or has the same characteristics as, the target procedure.

pending.C_F_PROCPOINTER-CPTR-c-funptr-scalar: Positive source control declares TYPE(C_FUNPTR) :: raw and passes raw as CPTR; companion checks C_NULL_FUNPTR remains null while raw from C_FUNLOC is non-null, with same-target and distinct-target procedure calls distinguished by sentinels; mutation passes TYPE(C_PTR) and claims no diagnostic facet.
pending.C_F_PROCPOINTER-CPTR-valid-procedure-add: Guarded positive source control first requires C_INT > 0, then covers both admitted CPTR sources: Fortran obtains CPTR from C_FUNLOC of a BIND(C) function returning sentinel 123_C_INT, and a mixed C companion defines int cf_twice(int x){return 2*x;} plus int (*cf_get(void))(int) returning its address; Fortran receives cf_get() as TYPE(C_FUNPTR), converts it with C_F_PROCPOINTER to a matching BIND(C) abstract interface, and asserts fp(21_C_INT)==42_C_INT. Mutation uses C_NULL_FUNPTR and treats non-association separately through C_ASSOCIATED, not as this restriction.
pending.C_F_PROCPOINTER-FPTR-procedure-pointer: Positive source control declares PROCEDURE(iface), POINTER :: fp and passes fp; mutation passes a nonpointer procedure designator and claims no diagnostic facet.
pending.C_F_PROCPOINTER-FPTR-not-coindexed-compo: OUT OF SCOPE: a coindexed FPTR component requires coarray/image execution, excluded by suite policy; source inventory records the restriction without a runtime fixture.
pending.C_F_PROCPOINTER-FPTR-compatible-interfac: Guarded positive source control first requires C_INT > 0, then uses an abstract BIND(C) interface integer(C_INT) function with one VALUE integer(C_INT) dummy matching the target; mutation changes only the result type in the FPTR interface and claims no diagnostic facet.

requirements.oracle: Source accounting only. Future fixtures initialize non-default sentinels before invoking the ISO_C_BINDING procedure and assert only portable single-image properties fixed by 18.2.3: pointer association status reached through the paired module procedure, exact integer kind and rank inquiries, exact character length and C_NULL_CHAR placement, exact sentinel values reached through an associated pointer, or equality with a companion C sizeof result. Argument shall-restrictions are source-control restrictions only and are not diagnostic facets unless a numbered constraint elsewhere requires rejection. Coindexed actual arguments remain out of scope for this single-image suite. Positive-control source controls are complete conforming fragments for their stated declarations and execution order; nonconforming source mutations are recorded only as load-bearing mutations, not as positive controls. Mixed Fortran/C plans rely on the suite's c_interop harness where companion C address or sizeof semantics are the portable oracle. Fixture plans first guard every ISO_C_BINDING kind constant with a positive availability test before declaring entities or writing literals of that kind; the unavailable branch performs no such declaration or literal write. C pointer association plans cover null, non-null, same-target, and distinct-target observations through C_ASSOCIATED or C helpers and never compare address values numerically. Array address plans use explicit nonzero lower bounds and hand-derived column-major expectations.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Source accounting only. This packet creates no Fortran fixture, compiler invocation, execution evidence, evidence link, fixture approval, oracle approval, or coverage claim. Grep of tests/ for C_F_PROCPOINTER, C_F_STRPOINTER, C_FUNLOC, C_LOC, C_SIZEOF, and F_C_STRING found incidental C_LOC/C_FUNLOC/C_F_POINTER uses in clause07 and clause10 and no fixture.json binding for these 18.2.3 procedures; no existing case is rebound here. Mixed Fortran/C plans use the c_interop harness only for C address and sizeof facts that are not fully observable from Fortran alone. No plan requires an exact malloc or raw storage-sequence round trip where processor-dependent association requirements control; such requirements are catalogue latitude rather than a portable value oracle.
requirements.dependencies: Registered dependencies: clauses 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, and 13 for source form, intrinsic types, declarations, expressions, pointer assignment, execution, procedure interfaces, and character data. Unregistered dependencies retained: 15.3 procedure characteristics and interoperability of procedure interfaces, 15.5 argument association, 16.9 inquiry intrinsics such as KIND, LEN, RANK and SIZE, 18.2.1-18.2.2 C types and named constants, 18.2.3.3 C_F_POINTER, 18.3 interoperability rules, companion C semantics, and clause 19 storage sequence terminology.

requirements.title: C_F_PROCPOINTER associates FPTR with the CPTR target
requirements.definition: On return, FPTR becomes pointer associated with the target of CPTR.

pending.C_F_PROCPOINTER-associated-target-callab: Guarded Fortran-only plan first requires C_INT > 0, defines a BIND(C) function add_sentinel(i) returning i+17_C_INT, takes raw=C_FUNLOC(add_sentinel), initializes PROCEDURE(iface), POINTER :: fp => NULL(), calls C_F_PROCPOINTER(raw,fp), asserts ASSOCIATED(fp), then calls fp(25_C_INT) and expects 42_C_INT; mutation omits C_F_PROCPOINTER so ASSOCIATED remains false.
pending.C_F_PROCPOINTER-associated-target-exact-: Guarded companion plan first requires C_INT > 0, uses two BIND(C) functions returning distinct sentinels 42_C_INT and -13_C_INT, converts the first with C_F_PROCPOINTER, and asserts the call result is 42_C_INT to prove the associated target is the CPTR target, not any compatible procedure.
